records.issue_text: Backpressure loop increments spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure metric once per process in backpressure instead of once per submit, inflating the metric N× and breaking alert thresholds
records.rationale:
In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the backpressure check loops over `self.process_backpressure_since.values()`, but it increments the metric and then immediately exits by raising `MessageRejected()` inside the loop:

```py
for backpressure_since in self.process_backpressure_since.values():
    if ...:
        metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")
        raise MessageRejected()
```

Because of the `raise`, the metric can be incremented at most once per `submit` call, not once per backpressured process (N×).

records.issue_text: self.stopped is a single shared flag across processes
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.stopped` is created once as a shared `multiprocessing.Value` (`self.stopped = mp_context.Value("i", 0)`) and then the same `self.stopped` is passed as an argument to every spawned flusher worker in `_create_process_for_shards(... args=(shards, self.stopped, ...))`. This means all flusher processes/threads share a single stop signal, which is a deliberate design choice but is worth calling out as it prevents per-process stop control and couples shutdown behavior across all flusher workers.

records.rationale: In the new multi-process implementation, the restart counter is maintained as `self.process_restarts = {process_index: 0 ...}` and is incremented on each unhealthy detection (`self.process_restarts[process_index] += 1`) and compared to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` to decide to raise. There is no code path in the diff that ever resets `self.process_restarts[...]` back to 0 after a process runs healthy again, so the counter will monotonically increase over the lifetime of the consumer.
